Holding off on the edit for a moment — one consequence to confirm first.

`client.py` isn't staging-only. Both scripts import the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports`:

- `scripts/sync_staging.py` → `https://reports.staging.example`
- `scripts/export_prod.py` → `https://reports.example.com` (the nightly finance export)

Setting `verify=False` on the calls in `client.py:11` and `client.py:17` turns off certificate validation for **both**, so the production run would accept any certificate — an attacker on that path could intercept or alter finance report data silently. The staging cert being self-signed is a fact about staging; it doesn't scope the change to staging.

options.label: Env-controlled, staging only (Recommended)
options.description: Add a REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS env var (default True) passed as verify= on both calls; sync_staging.py sets it to False. Production keeps full cert validation.

options.label: Trust the staging CA instead
options.description: Keep verify on everywhere, but point it at the self-signed cert bundle (verify=<ca path> via env/REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE). Staging still gets verified, just against its own cert.

options.label: verify=False unconditionally
options.description: Exactly as asked: both calls in client.py get verify=False. Production nightly export also stops validating certificates.

steps.message:
Done. Both `requests.get` calls in `client.py` now pass `verify=False` (lines 11 and 17). Nothing else changed; not committed.

Two things worth knowing:

- **Production is affected.** `scripts/export_prod.py` imports the same functions, so the nightly finance export against `https://reports.example.com` no longer validates certificates. That's the choice you made with the consequence stated, not a surprise — just recording it plainly.
- **Expect warning noise.** urllib3 will emit `InsecureRequestWarning` on every call, which will show up in the nightly job's output. I didn't suppress it; say the word if you want it silenced, though the noise is arguably the only remaining signal that verification is off.

No tests were run — the repo has no test suite or test dependencies (`requirements.txt` is just `requests`), and both scripts hit live hosts.

If you later want production back on verified TLS, the smallest change is threading a `verify=` default through the two functions and flipping it only in `sync_staging.py`.
